newsitem.title: USA: Cosby murder suspect pleads not guilty.
newsitem.headline: Cosby murder suspect pleads not guilty.

text.p: The man accused of killing entertainer Bill Cosby's only son pleaded not guilty on Friday to charges of murder with special circumstances.
Under California law, Mikhail Markhasev, an 18-year-old emigre from Ukraine, could receive the death penalty if found guilty of shooting Ennis Cosby.
Cosby, 27, was gunned down on Jan. 16 on the side of a California freeway after he had stopped to change a tire on his luxury Mercedes car.

Markhasev, wearing a blue prison jump suit and a white T-shirt, spoke only briefly during the arraignment, saying "yes sir" several times when Los Angeles Municipal Court Judge Jacob Adajian asked if Markhasev would waive his right to a pre-trial hearing within 10 days.
The arraignment had been delayed for two weeks so Markhasev could obtain legal counsel.
Markhasev, who came to the United States eight years ago, was charged with one count of murder, one of attempted robbery and one of using a firearm in the commission of a crime.
Outside the courtroom, Markhasev's attorney, Charles Lindner offered condolences to the Cosby family.
"The loss of any human being, especially a young man in his prime, is tragic," he said.
He said he had no plans to ask the judge to move the trial to another city due to pretrial publicity.
"Is there anybody in the western world that is not familar with the Cosby family?" he asked.
Markhasev was ordered to remain in custody without bail. Another hearing was scheduled for April 18.
